locator: I q.2 a.3 co., quarta via: Quod autem dicitur maxime tale in aliquo genere, est causa omnium quae sunt illius generis
interpretation: Stated, as in the text, for any genus, read as any perfection; the maximum causes the perfection in every other thing that has it (fire, maximally hot, causes all hot things). The maximum itself is excluded: fire is not said to cause its own heat. Only the instance for being (esse) is used. Aquinas says 'ut in eodem libro dicitur', but Metaphysics II.1, 993b24-26 argues the converse (the cause of a quality in others is most such); the principle is therefore attributed to Aquinas, and its truth for non-transcendental genera (the fire example) is a known weak point that the reading does not hide.
